title: Enabled 2-to-4 decoder
goal: Show the four active-high minterms selected by an enable and two select inputs.

rubric.must: The E input visibly fans out to logic feeding all four outputs.
Y0, Y1, Y2, and Y3 visibly correspond respectively to E·S1bar·S0bar, E·S1bar·S0, E·S1·S0bar, and E·S1·S0.
Visible inverter gates create complemented S1 and S0 signals.
Four distinct outputs labelled Y0 through Y3 appear.
Branches of the enable and select signals are visually unambiguous.

ideal.notes: Gate-level enabled 2-to-4 decoder in ANSI/IEEE Std 91 distinctive-shape symbols. Enable E and select lines S1 and S0 enter as labelled stubs on the left. Two inverters produce the complements nS1 and nS0. E is qualified by S1 and by nS1 in a pair of AND gates, giving the half-decode nets e0 and e1, and each of those is combined with S0 or nS0 in a final AND to give one of the four active-high outputs Y0 to Y3. The S0 and nS0 literals run as vertical rails tapped twice each; all wires are orthogonal, filled dots mark junctions and plain crossings mark wires that pass without connecting. Drawn in the idiom of the logic exemplar: ANSI/IEEE Std 91 distinctive shapes on one body box so the columns line up, ink-only palette with paper-filled gate bodies so a wire passing behind a gate is visibly interrupted, the gate type carried by the outline rather than printed under it, and the label slot spent on net names instead. Row pitch, channel x and canvas size are solved from browser-measured text widths, and the drawing was checked label-against-label, label-against-wire, label-against-canvas-edge and wire-against-every-unattached-gate before it was written: 0 collisions, and no wire crosses a gate body.
